text:
elaine.docs: heads-up: I opened a small docs PR to soften SOC2 retention phrasing and add an SDK migration note for export/state changes. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1011

mina-legal: Thanks. Please avoid wording that suggests immediate user-driven deletion of SOC2 evidence. Use phrases like 'restricts automated deletion' or 'access-controlled until disposition'.

elaine.docs: noted — drafting with 'restricts automated deletion' language. Also adding a short table that maps API fields -> operator behavior for clarity.

carol-sre: can we include an ops note about the cleanup worker? We mark exports with status and a tombstone time; the worker skips records with hold=true. That helps infra folks understand the difference between 'retention_seconds' and 'hold'.

elaine.docs: good call. I'll add a one-paragraph "how it works" under the export docs: "cleanup worker filters by export.metadata.hold == true; otherwise it enqueues deletion when retention window elapses."

hugo-ux: from a UX perspective, SDKs should bubble up a human-friendly reason when an export is blocked by legal hold (e.g., 'Held for legal review — contact legal@'). Could we include message samples for SDK authors to show in UI?

tony-pe: yes — add a sample mapping in the migration guide: export.status -> user_message. Eg: {"held":"This export is currently held for compliance review. Contact legal@..."}.

julian: also add example response body for the new 'restricted' state so clients can detect it programmatically:
```json
{"export_id":"exp_def456","status":"restricted","legal_hold":true,"hold_reason":"litigation","retention_seconds":0}
```

elaine.docs: adding that exact JSON sample. I'm writing the SDK migration section to recommend: 1) treat status in ["ready","processing","restricted","failed"] 2) show friendly message when restricted, 3) offer a 'request review' flow that opens a support ticket.

carol-sre: tiny runtime note: the 'hold_reason' is freeform for now but ops will normalize a few enums. I'll add a comment in the doc: "hold_reason may be freeform; use legal_hold boolean for enforcement checks."

mina-legal: For SOC2 wording: prefer "retention policy governs automated deletion of exports; legal holds suspend automated deletion pending disposition." Can we include that sentence verbatim in the PR?

elaine.docs: will do. Draft snippet placed under "Retention & legal holds" section. Also adding code samples for curl/python/ruby for creating an export with redaction toggles:

```bash
# curl example: create export with 14d retention and redact=true
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"scope":"audit_export","retention_seconds":1209600,"redact_pii":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/exports
```

```python
# python: check export status and handle restricted state
resp = client.create_export(scope='audit_export', retention_seconds=1209600, redact_pii=True)
status = client.get_export(resp['export_id'])
if status.get('legal_hold'):
    show_message("This export is held for compliance review. Contact legal@redwood.ai")
```

```ruby
# ruby: create export and log response
res = client.create_export({scope: 'audit_export', retention_seconds: 1209600, redact_pii: true})
puts res.to_json
```

tony-pe: also add a small migration note for older SDKs: if client sees unknown status values, fall back to a generic UI state "Export pending review" rather than crashing.

elaine.docs: added a one-line migration note: "Handle unknown status strings defensively; treat as pending and surface contact info."

compliance-bot: Reminder: run the SOC2 linter and tag @legal-review in the PR. Also include a changelog entry summarizing the user-facing wording change.

elaine.docs: done the linter locally, tagging @legal-review — changelog entry added: "clarify retention semantics; document legal hold behavior and add SDK migration examples."

julian: LGTM from engineering examples. Once legal confirms tiny wording tweak, we can land. I like the user-message samples for UX.

elaine.docs: thanks everyone. I'll merge after legal signoff and then file a follow-up to backport the snippets to the SDK repo READMEs.
